title: No commercial small modular reactor has yet operated in a Western country, and the first United States project was cancelled in 2023
oneLiner: The designs being licensed overseas remain unbuilt; the most advanced US project collapsed on cost.
body: Small modular reactors operate in Russia and China under state programs. In the United States, the NuScale project for a Utah utility consortium was cancelled in November 2023 after its estimated power price rose and subscribers withdrew. No Western SMR has reached commercial operation.
contextBackground: The state of small modular reactor deployment is the factual test of the 'keep the option open' argument. Both sides accept the record; they differ on whether it describes a technology that is early or one that is failing.
contextDisagreement: Not disputed as fact. Supporters of SMRs argue first-of-a-kind cancellations are normal and later designs are progressing; critics argue the cancellation revealed costs no later design has yet escaped.

evidenceItems.citation: World Nuclear Association, Small Nuclear Power Reactors — status of designs and projects

otherClaim.title: The ban stops the market from finding cheaper and faster routes to nuclear, such as small modular reactors

claimItself.title: The ban stops the market from finding cheaper and faster routes to nuclear, such as small modular reactors
claimItself.oneLiner: A prohibition rules out every future design, not just today's large plants.
claimItself.body: Cost and timeline estimates for nuclear are estimates for large reactors built once. Small modular designs promise factory production, shorter builds and smaller sites, and several are in licensing overseas. A legislated ban means no Australian proponent can test those promises against local conditions, however the technology develops.
